best_for: Teams on Windows that still keep code or documents in Subversion and want commits, logs and diffs from File Explorer.

points.title: Everything for the client side
points.text: TortoiseSVN brings what you need to work with a Subversion repository. You only install the separate Subversion package if you want to run a server.

points.title: Free, even at work
points.text: It is GPL licensed and free for anyone, including in a commercial setting, with no restrictions.

points.title: Tools in the box
points.text: Besides the Explorer menus and status overlays, it bundles TortoiseMerge, TortoiseBlame, TortoiseIDiff and SubWCRev, plus a revision graph and issue tracker links. It speaks http, https, svn, svn+ssh and file.

points.title: Overlay icons can run out
points.text: Windows allows only 15 overlay icons in total. Cloud apps such as OneDrive use some, so TortoiseSVN's status icons may not all appear.

points.title: Admin to install, reboot to upgrade
points.text: Installing needs administrator rights, but daily use does not. An upgrade installs over the old version, then wants a reboot or at least a sign-out.

points.title: Match the build to Windows
points.text: There are 32-bit, 64-bit and Arm64 installers, and 44 language packs. On 64-bit Windows, use the 64-bit build so the menus appear in Explorer.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. The listing keeps 8 versions, all machine-wide installs.
